---
title: "Reviewing articles for journals"
date: 2023-05-12
description: "How reviewing invitations usually arise, and where to find training."
categories: [Research career]
aliases: ["/reviewing-article/"]
---

After building a research profile on sites like ORCID, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, Scopus or PubMed, an editor will typically notice your work and invite you to review a manuscript, or to review for the journal regularly.

Some journals also call for applications, especially from early career researchers, to join as reviewers or editors. Long-term association with a journal (doing well in the tasks given, and sending helpful reviews on time) can earn a place on the editorial board.

## Places to look

- [ABCD index](https://abcdindex.com/): possibly a way to apply to become a reviewer.
- Taylor & Francis [peer review training programme](https://editorresources.taylorandfrancis.com/reviewer-guidelines/peer-review-training/#upcomingevents).
- Dove Medical Press [reviewer training programme](https://www.dovepress.com/peer-review-guidelines/reviewer-training-programme).
- F1000Research uses a [different review process](https://f1000research.com/for-authors/peer-review) from the usual one.
- PLOS has [excellent resources for reviewers](https://plos.org/resources/for-reviewers/).
